title: Mogao Caves
summary: The Mogao Caves are a Buddhist cave-temple complex cut into a cliff south-east of the Dunhuang oasis in Gansu. UNESCO dates their first construction to 366 CE, while Getty calls that date a legend, and building continued into the 14th century. About 492 caves survive; in 1900 a sealed Library Cave with nearly 50,000 manuscripts and textiles was opened.

uncertainty.note: 366 is the date UNESCO gives for first construction; Getty reports it as legend. The end is "the 14th century" in both sources, taken as 1400.

where.historical_name: Mogaoku ("peerless caves"), also called the Caves of the Thousand Buddhas, on the Silk Road at Dunhuang; the ruling polity changed over its thousand years of use

importance.justification: UNESCO meets all six cultural criteria; the site is described as the largest and longest used treasure house of Buddhist art.

sources.title: 14 Facts about the Cave Temples of Dunhuang

reviewer_note: Least sure of the start date: 366 is traditional (a monk's vision), with UNESCO stating it as the first construction. The end is "the 14th century", not a year.
